exposure: prenatal Polybrominated Diphenyl Ethers (PBDEs) concentrations (nine congeners)
outcome: thyroid hormones (THs) in cord plasma (TSH, total T4, free T4, total T3, free T3)
children's neurobehavioral development (Child Behavior Checklist scores for Somatic Complaints, Withdrawn, Sleep Problems, Internalizing Problems, Attention Problems)
cohort: Mother-child pairs from the Shanghai-Minhang Birth Cohort Study, with 199-339 pairs included in the final analyses depending on the specific outcome and follow-up time.
finding: Prenatal PBDE concentrations were positively associated with various neurobehavioral problems in children (differing by sex) and inversely associated with thyroid hormones in cord plasma, though THs did not explain the neurotoxic impact of PBDEs on neurobehavior.
